title: OxCAM workholding template (workholding.json inside a .ocamhold archive), version 4
description: A fixture made of STEP parts (stored beside this document as bodies/<sha256>.step, or among a project's models) in shared template coordinates, in millimetres. Each part is carried by the fixed base or by a member that moves along a line within its travel range (linked members follow another member's travel times their ratio, along their own direction). Datums are named points with a direction: picked on a part's face, edge or vertex (moving with the part's member; 'point' and 'direction' are its geometry as modelled), typed (moving with 'member'), offset from another datum along template X, Y, Z or that datum's direction, or the midpoint of two. Holdings say where the stock sits: between two jaw faces (its side on face_a, its bottom grip_depth below the 'seat' datum), on a dovetail (flanks face_a and face_b, its shoulder on the seat, its tenon depth below it), at a seat frame (origin and Z from 'seat', X from 'x_datum'; the stock box point 'anchor' there, per axis 0 = min, 1 = middle, 2 = max), or in a chuck (a bar centred on the 'axis' datum, gripped on its diameter by the jaw face face_a, whose distance from the axis is the radius gripped; its end grip_depth behind the plane of 'seat', the front of the jaws facing out of the chuck; with no member moving face_a, a collet, bars up to grip_range smaller than its bore). 'mount' is the datum the workholding sits on the machine by. Version 1 documents (bodies with jaw roles, one datum frame, an opening range) are migrated when read; version 2 documents are version 3 documents without chucks; version 3 documents are version 4 documents without jaw mounts or jaw sets. Version 4: a chuck may say how jaws go on its master jaws ('jaw_mount': the interface by name, a label a setup matches jaw sets by, and the datum on master jaw 1 where a jaw's seat goes, its direction out of the chuck); its own top jaws ('top_jaw' parts) are left out when a setup puts a jaw set on. A jaw set ('jaw_set': one jaw's parts, copied onto each master jaw) says its interface, whether it is a hard jaw with grip steps or a soft blank to be bored, its front, and its 'options', the ways it goes on (a jaw that goes on either way round is two options, as a vise's holdings are its ways of holding): each a name, the datum that seats on the master jaw (its direction out of the chuck), which way is in towards the chuck's axis, and its steps: a gripping face (its normal says whether it grips an outside or an inside diameter) and the face the work's end stops against. A jaw set has no holdings. An earlier draft of version 4 also wrote a mount's 'pitch' and 'positions' and a set's one 'seat', 'inward' and 'steps': the first two are ignored, the others read as one option named 'Normal'. See docs/design-log/0035-workholding-templates.md.

seat.description: An earlier draft's single way on, read as an option named 'Normal'.
